description.narrative: This project establishes a new USFWS MENTOR Signature Initiative to develop the capacity of a transdisciplinary team of conservationists from Central African nations who by working together will create dedicated research, management and conservation actions for the African manatee. The project is intended to conserve the African manatee (Trichechus sengalensis) by training and mentoring a team of manatee conservationists who can problem solve together and determine innovative approaches to addressing threats such as high levels of direct bushmeat hunting, incidental capture in fishing nets, hydroelectric and agricultural dams that isolate populations and kill manatees in their control structures, and increasing habitat destruction. Specific activities include: 1) identifying the team of eight MENTOR-Manatee Fellows who are already enrolled in formal educational programs in Central Africa, 2) conducting training at field sites on team building and conflict management, practical experience in the field (conducting boat and interview surveys, a manatee necropsy, sample collection, use and care of field equipment), data entry and analysis, program design and adaptive management, stakeholder relationship building, communication / media, law enforcement, educational outreach, project planning and adaptive management,3) determining team projects, 4) providing on-going mentoring, and 5) implementing projects and conducting evaluation.
